text:
max: heads up — we're getting a customer escalation: p95 latency in eu-west up ~3x since 08:15 UTC. ticket #INC-7892 opened by support-bot :rotating_light:

carmen: seeing it too on dashboards, per-route p95 for /v1/generate jumped from 120ms -> 420ms around 08:14. p99 also climbing.

oliver: traces show TLS handshake timeouts and an extra ~40-60ms in DNS resolution on many requests. grabbing packet captures now.

maya: @max can you paste the top traces? I want to see client -> edge -> backend hop list.

max: pasted sample trace (sensitive fields redacted):
```
client -> edge-eu-west-3 (34.56.78.90) : tcp syn 1ms
edge-eu-west-3 -> upstream-router (10.200.5.12) : tcp syn ack 8ms
edge-eu-west-3 TLS handshake: 120ms (cert verify 80ms)
backend connection: 30ms
total request time: 410ms
```

oliver: digging into DNS — multiple resolves for api.redwood-inference.com returning IPv6 + IPv4; some clients try ipv6 then fallback to ipv4, adding ~50ms. Also saw EDNS reponses with truncated flag occasionally.

carmen: strange — our DNS TTLs haven't changed. Could be resolver-side throttling or a route-multipath causing extra RTTs. Any signs of route flaps from provider?

infra-bot: automated note — CDN provider reported a config push to eu POPs at 08:10 UTC (ref: https://status.cdn.example/incident/345).

max: that aligns with timeline. provider noted "edge config distribution" — possible ephemeral inconsistency in load balancing weights across POPs.

natalie: reproducer steps for support engineers:
1) curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup}\ntime_connect:%{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect:%{time_appconnect}\ntime_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
2) run `dig +noall +answer api.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8`
3) traceroute to resolved ip (tcp/443)

max: example `dig` output we captured:```
api.redwood-inference.com. 60 IN A 34.56.78.90
api.redwood-inference.com. 60 IN AAAA 2604:1f18:abcd::1
;; flags: qr rd ad; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 2, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
```
But occasionally clients saw no AAAA then had to fallback, causing extra connect time.

oliver: packet capture reveals a subset of edge nodes returning RST during TLS renegotiation with some backends — likely an inter-pop routing mismatch. When handshake retries occur, client-perceived TLS time jumps from ~10ms -> 150-300ms.

carmen: mitigation options:
- roll back recent CDN config push (coordinate with provider)
- temporarily force resolver policy to prefer IPv4 for affected POPs (quick local fix)
- route small % of traffic to standby eu-west-2 nodes with known stable path

maya: can we quickly test forcing IPv4 with a host header test? i.e. `curl --ipv4 -vS https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate` and compare times. If IPv4 consistently avoids the spike, that's a good mitigation.

max: ran test from our synthetic runner in eu-west-1: IPv4 p95=130ms, IPv6 p95=410ms (same spike). Good signal.

natalie: I opened support ticket with CDN (ticket #CDN-1123) and attached packet captures + traceroutes. Asked them to check configuration convergence across EU POPs and if any L3 changes were rolled out at 08:10.

infra-bot: action log — created incident channel #incident-eu-edge-dns-latency and added oncall.

oliver: quick workaround we pushed: updated edge-level resolver policy to prefer A over AAAA for 15m via feature flag (ff.edge.dns_prefer_ipv4=true). Observed immediate p95 reduction from 420ms -> 160ms for Canary traffic.

carmen: good. pushing to 10% traffic now and monitoring. Also added a temporary panic weight to route 5% to eu-west-2 (lower latency).

max: reminder — need to communicate to support team with repro steps and ETA. I've drafted customer-facing note: "We've identified a config rollout at our edge provider causing inconsistent route selection and delayed TLS handshakes for a subset of EU traffic. We've applied a temporary mitigation and are working with the provider on a full rollback/convergence. Will update in 30m."

maya: monitoring — Grafana panel `edge.dns.latency.p95` now shows improvement for canaries. Still watching p99 for any residual TLS spikes.

natalie: long-term follow-ups:
- ask CDN for RCA and ensure future rollouts have staged POP convergence checks
- add e2e synthetic tests for ipv6->ipv4 fallbacks in eu regions
- add alert rule when DNS resolution time > 30ms for >1% of requests
- evaluate forcing EDNS buffer sizes on resolver if fragmentation observed

oliver: added a small patch to our runtime to prefer cached A records when handshake times spike — will open PR with tests.

carmen: timeline note: root cause appears to be inconsistent route/weight distribution on provider side leading to mixed IPv6/A path selection and occasional edge->backend handshake resets during the rollout.

max: next update in 25m after full 10% rollout. tagging @support-bot to post customer update then.

support-bot: posted update to ticket #INC-7892: "Temporary mitigation applied; working with CDN on full rollback. Next update in ~25m." :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks team. keep logs/pcaps attached to incident channel. once CDN confirms rollback we'll do a controlled revert of the feature flag.

max: closing loop — if anyone sees reappearance or p99 > 800ms, escalate to paging channel immediately.

oliver: will follow up with extracted traceroutes and a short writeup for postmortem.

natalie: adding checklist items to postmortem draft: dns reproduction steps, CDN ticket id, mitigation timeline, customer comms.

max: good work.
